tldr: Get a baseline first. Then take two paths in parallel: who your users are, and what they do. Write your hypotheses before you go looking, time-box every behavioural one, and once you find the behaviour that separates retained users, push more users into it.

Then push more users into the winning behavior
How do you push more users into the winning behaviour?
faq: Where do you start with a retention problem?
A baseline. Until you know what your retention curve actually looks like — and over what window — you can't tell whether anything you ship moved it.
Who your users are (their characteristics) and what they do (their behaviour). Retained and non-retained users usually differ on both, and the two paths surface different kinds of fix.
Why write hypotheses before looking at the data?
Because otherwise you'll find something. Data explored without a hypothesis produces a pattern every time, and most of them are noise.
Because "users who do X retain better" is meaningless without a window. Doing X in the first session and doing it in month three are different claims with different fixes.
